meta.location: The wall of Zarahemla, and then the whole land
principles: A sermon that divides its hearers
An argument built out of resentment

world_behind.title: The crowd splits three ways
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has believers going to Nephi, verse 2 has others throwing stones and arrows, and verse 3 has more believing when the throwing fails. Helaman 13:2 records the same city casting Samuel out before he ever climbed the wall, so this crowd has already refused him once.

world_behind.title: Nephi is already working
world_behind.text: Verses 4 and 5 have Nephi baptizing, prophesying, showing signs, and telling people things beforehand so they will remember having been told. Helaman 10:17 had the Spirit carrying him from multitude to multitude; six chapters later he is stationary and the people are coming to him.

world_behind.title: The failure to hit him is used as evidence against him
world_behind.text: Verse 6 has them concluding he has a devil, since nothing else explains the misses. Alma 30:53 has Korihor report that the devil appeared to him as an angel, and 3 Nephi 2:2 has the next generation credit the signs of Christ's birth to the devil's power. The explanation is a standing one in this part of the record.

world_behind.title: Samuel leaves and is never mentioned again
world_behind.text: Verses 7 and 8 have him jumping off the wall, going home to preach, and dropping out of the Nephite record entirely.

world_behind.title: Four years pass with little change
world_behind.text: Verses 9 through 12 summarize the eighty-seventh through eighty-ninth years in three sentences. Helaman 11:36 to 38 had disposed of four years the same way a few chapters earlier, so the compression is Mormon's habit at the end of a book rather than a gap in his source.

world_behind.title: Angels appear to wise men
world_behind.text: Verse 14 reports it in the ninetieth year, in the language Luke 2:10 uses at Bethlehem.

world_behind.title: The unbelievers' reasoning is quoted in full
world_behind.text: Verses 16 through 21 give their argument, including a theory about priests keeping them ignorant and dependent. Alma 30:27 has Korihor make the same charge against the Nephite high priest, and 2 Nephi 28:5 and 6 has Nephi predict the sayings almost word for word.

words.text: A dismissive way of naming a man. The word stands in seven verses of this record, and in five of them it is a compound meaning a companion, as in "fellow beings" at Mosiah 2:17 and "fellow laborers" at Alma 31:32. Only two verses use it as a bare noun for a person, this one and Mosiah 13:1, where Noah's priests call Abinadi "this fellow." Both are hostile.
A change in condition. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, where the record has almost nothing to report for a year.
Arrived at by chance rather than knowledge. It appears a single time in all of scripture, here, in the unbelievers' explanation of how the prophets could be right.
Lack of knowledge, here alleged as a condition imposed by others. The record uses the word seven times, twice in this chapter, and Alma 30:23 has Korihor making the same charge against the priests.
Beyond understanding, and in this verse suspiciously so. Scripture carries the word just once, in the phrase "the cunning and the mysterious arts of the evil one."
Reports spread without a source. The record uses the word eight times and the King James Bible never. Verse 22 makes Satan the one spreading them across the land.

phrases.term: As many as believed on his word went forth and sought for Nephi
phrases.text: The believers go looking for a different prophet. Samuel gave them the message and Nephi had the baptizing authority.

phrases.term: They could not hit him with their stones neither with their arrows
phrases.text: The event the whole chapter turns on. It is a miracle of failure rather than of display.

phrases.term: When they saw that they could not hit him, there were many more who did believe
phrases.text: One group's reading of the misses. Verse 6 gives another group's reading of the same fact.

phrases.term: That they might know and remember at the time of their coming that they had been made known unto them beforehand
phrases.text: Nephi's stated purpose in prophesying. The point of the advance notice is what it will mean afterward.

phrases.term: Take this fellow and bind him, for behold he hath a devil
phrases.text: The alternative explanation. The unexplained protection becomes proof of the opposite conclusion.

phrases.term: He did cast himself down from the wall, and did flee out of their lands
phrases.text: The exit. He goes home and preaches to his own people, and the record follows him no further.

phrases.term: He was never heard of more among the Nephites
phrases.text: The record closing a file. One of its most quoted prophets leaves in a single clause.

phrases.term: Angels did appear unto men, wise men, and did declare unto them glad tidings of great joy
phrases.text: Reported in the ninetieth year, in the same words Luke uses at Bethlehem (Luke 2:10). Both hemispheres get angels and wise men.

phrases.term: Some things they may have guessed right, among so many
phrases.text: The first argument: enough predictions will produce some hits. It concedes the accuracy and denies what it implies.

phrases.term: Why will he not show himself in this land as well as in the land of Jerusalem?
phrases.text: The second argument, and a fair question. 3 Nephi 11 answers it in about thirty years.

phrases.term: Thus will they keep us in ignorance if we will yield ourselves unto them
phrases.text: The third argument: the whole thing is a device for control. Korihor had made the same case in Alma 30:23.

verses.label: v. 4–5
verses.title: A second preacher named, and what he was doing
verses.text: The new believers are sent somewhere specific: "they went away unto Nephi to be baptized." The record then describes his work in a chain of participles, "baptizing, and prophesying, and preaching, crying repentance unto the people, showing signs and wonders, working miracles among the people," and gives the purpose of the signs in verse 5, "that they might know and remember at the time of their coming that they had been made known unto them beforehand." Signs are described as memory aids for a later date.

verses.label: v. 6–8
verses.title: A prophet jumps off a wall and leaves the record
verses.text: The escape is physical and undignified: "as they went forth to lay their hands on him, behold, he did cast himself down from the wall, and did flee out of their lands, yea, even unto his own country." Verse 8 then closes the account with a formula the volume uses of three people: "he was never heard of more among the Nephites." Alma 45:18 says it of Alma and Alma 63:8 of the ships that sailed north. The man whose prophecies drive the next four chapters walks out of the book in one clause.

verses.label: v. 9–13
verses.title: Four years reported almost entirely as year-endings
verses.text: The record spends four verses closing years and says outright that there is nothing in them: "thus ended also the eighty and seventh year," "these were the conditions also, in the eighty and eighth year," and then verse 12, "there was but little alteration in the affairs of the people, save it were the people began to be more hardened in iniquity." Only at verse 13, in the ninetieth year, does content arrive. A book that will spend nine chapters on the events of the next few years first shows four in which almost nothing happens.

verses.label: v. 16
verses.title: The sceptics' best argument, quoted
verses.text: The record puts a genuine objection in its opponents' mouths and does not weaken it: "Some things they may have guessed right, among so many; but behold, we know that all these great and marvelous works cannot come to pass, of which has been spoken." The reasoning is statistical. Given enough predictions, some will match by chance, and the ones that match prove nothing about the rest. The record reproduces the argument in a single sentence and offers no reply to it in this chapter.

verses.label: v. 18–20
verses.title: A geographic objection, and a charge of manipulation
verses.text: Two more arguments are quoted in the same block. The first is about location: "why will he not show himself in this land as well as in the land of Jerusalem?" The second is about motive, and it accuses the tradition of being a tool: "we know that this is a wicked tradition, which has been handed down unto us by our fathers, to cause us that we should believe in some great and marvelous thing which should come to pass... that thereby they may keep us in ignorance." The record preserves the accusation that religion is being used for control, stated by people inside the book.

chapter.title: The same fact produces opposite conclusions
chapter.text: The stones miss. Verse 3 has people believing because of it and verse 6 has people diagnosing a devil because of it.

chapter.title: Belief sends them to a different man
chapter.text: Verse 1 has Samuel's converts going to find Nephi. The messenger and the ordinance are held by two people, and neither competes with the other.

chapter.title: The record loses track of its own prophet
chapter.text: Verse 8 says he was never heard of more. One of the most quoted figures in the book exits without a summary.

chapter.title: Almost nothing happens for four years
chapter.text: Verses 9 through 12 compress them into three sentences, and "little alteration" is the chapter's own phrase for it.

chapter.title: The unbelievers get a full hearing
chapter.text: Six verses are given to their reasoning in their own voice. Mormon quotes the case rather than only naming it.

chapter.title: The strongest objection is the fairest one
chapter.text: Verse 19 asks why Christ would appear at Jerusalem and not here. 3 Nephi 11 gives the answer, which nobody in this chapter lives to hear.

chapter.title: The theory of control is old
chapter.text: Alma 30:23 had Korihor arguing that priests keep the people in ignorance. The same case reappears sixty years later in the mouths of ordinary citizens.

chapter.title: The book ends in the year before the sign
chapter.text: The ninetieth year closes with Satan holding the hearts of the people, two years before the night with no darkness.

applications.title: Send people where the help actually is
applications.text: Samuel preached and pointed them to Nephi for baptism. Knowing which part of the work is yours is part of doing it.

applications.title: One event does not settle anything
applications.text: When the stones and the arrows kept missing, many more believed and went to be baptized, while others called for him to be seized. What people already wanted usually decides how they read the thing they just watched.

applications.title: Notice when you are explaining away rather than explaining
applications.text: The misses got attributed to a devil. When a fact is inconvenient, watch for the account that keeps everything else unchanged.

applications.title: Do the work and then go home
applications.text: Samuel cast himself down from the wall, returned to his own country, and was never heard of again among the Nephites. Finishing an assignment sometimes means leaving without seeing what it produced.

applications.title: Watch what happens when nothing happens
applications.text: "Little alteration" covered a year of quiet hardening. Drift does not announce itself.

applications.title: Watch for the argument from the base rate
applications.text: Their answer was that some things may have been guessed right among so many. The principle is a real one, and here it was doing the work of dismissing every specific claim without examining any of them.

applications.title: Take the good objection seriously
applications.text: Why here and not there is a real question. Dismissing the best version of an argument leaves it standing.

applications.title: Be careful when suspicion becomes the whole account
applications.text: They reasoned that the tradition existed to keep them ignorant and dependent on their teachers. A theory that explains why nothing can be checked has disposed of its own test, which is a reason to trust it less rather than more.

questions.text: What evidence have I seen that changed my mind?
What have I attributed to a bad motive because the plain reading was inconvenient?
Who did the work in my life and then disappeared without credit?
What year of mine had little alteration, and what was happening under it?
Where am I calling a pattern a coincidence?
What is the strongest objection to something I believe?
Whose teaching do I resent depending on?
